speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please tell me how long you have been experiencing wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions, and if you have noticed any joint swelling or stiffness.

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection (DGI).

The combination of a 3-day history of migratory polyarthralgia (left knee), followed by oligoarticular arthritis (left wrist), chills, malaise, and a recent camping trip in Minnesota (risk for tick-borne diseases) in a sexually active 17-year-old male is highly suggestive of DGI. While Lyme disease is a consideration given the location and history, the specific progression of migratory joint pain to a single joint with systemic symptoms strongly points to gonococcal infection. I will request a Urine_NGC_PCR test to confirm the diagnosis.
